name: Congenital Cataract Microcornea with Corneal Opacity

criteria.description: Presence of cataract detected at birth or within the first year of life
Corneal diameter smaller than 10 mm in newborns or less than 11 mm in infants
Presence of corneal opacity affecting visual axis confirmed by slit-lamp examination
Positive family history of congenital cataract or microcornea
No evidence of systemic syndromic involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (congenital cataract, microcornea, and corneal opacity) must be present for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by ophthalmological examination; genetic testing may aid in differential diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Lens opacity present at birth or early infancy
Opacity involving the cornea, often affecting the visual axis

common.notes: Involuntary eye movement due to visual impairment

occasional.notes: Elevated intraocular pressure secondary to anterior segment anomalies
Decreased vision due to abnormal visual development
Abnormal blood vessel growth into the cornea
Developmental anomalies of the anterior eye structures

rare.notes: Separation of the retina from underlying tissue

laboratory: Genetic testing for mutations in crystallin and connexin genes
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing cataract and corneal opacity
Ultrasound biomicroscopy for anterior segment evaluation
other: Visual evoked potentials may show delayed responses due to visual pathway impairment

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic features such as developmental delay or skeletal anomalies
Central corneal opacity with iridocorneal adhesions

redFlags: Rapidly progressive corneal opacity leading to complete vision loss
Signs of secondary glaucoma with elevated intraocular pressure
Presence of systemic abnormalities suggesting syndromic involvement
references: Orphanet: Congenital cataract microcornea with corneal opacity - ORPHA:289499
Shiels A, Hejtmancik JF. Molecular genetics of cataract. Prog Mol Biol Transl Sci. 2015;134:203-218.
Reddy MA, Francis PJ, Berry V, et al. Microcornea-cataract syndrome: clinical and molecular genetic studies. Ophthalmology. 2004;111(10):1870-1876.
